events.label: Watson has not heard Holmes refer to his relations or early life until Holmes later begins talking about his brother

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: he began to talk to Watson about his brother

events.label: Holmes and Watson discuss atavism and hereditary aptitudes after tea on a summer evening
Watson says Holmes's observational and deductive faculty are due to systematic training

communicates.speaker: character_john_watson
communicates.content: from all that you have told me, it seems obvious that your faculty of observation and your peculiar facility for deduction are due to your own systematic training.

events.label: Holmes responds that he is considering it to some extent

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: To some extent

events.label: Holmes states his ancestors were country squires and his turn that way is in his veins via his grandmother Vernet

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My ancestors were country squires... my turn that way is in my veins, and may have come with my grandmother, who was the sister of Vernet, the French artist. Art in the blood is liable to take the strangest forms.

events.label: Watson asks how Holmes knows the trait is hereditary

communicates.speaker: character_john_watson
communicates.content: But how do you know that it is hereditary?

events.label: Holmes says Mycroft possesses the trait in a larger degree

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Because my brother Mycroft possesses it in a larger degree than I do.

events.label: Watson asks why Mycroft is unknown to police or the public

communicates.speaker: character_john_watson
communicates.content: If there were another man with such singular powers in England, how was it that neither police nor public had heard of him?

events.label: Watson asks implying Holmes acknowledges his brother as superior
Holmes laughs at Watson's suggestion about modesty
Holmes states he cannot agree that modesty is a virtue and claims his statements are exact truth

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My dear Watson, I cannot agree with those who rank modesty among the virtues... When I say, therefore, that Mycroft has better powers of observation than I, you may take it that I am speaking the exact and literal truth.

events.label: Watson asks if Mycroft is Holmes's junior

communicates.speaker: character_john_watson
communicates.content: Is he your junior?

events.label: Holmes says Mycroft is seven years his senior

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Seven years my senior.

events.label: Holmes says Mycroft is well known in his own circle and mentions the Diogenes Club

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Oh, he is very well known in his own circle. Well, in the Diogenes Club, for example.

events.label: Holmes checks his watch and invites Watson to meet two curiosities at the club

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The Diogenes Club is the queerest club in London, and Mycroft one of the queerest men... It's six now, so if you care for a stroll this beautiful evening I shall be very happy to introduce you to two curiosities.

events.label: Holmes and Watson walk towards Regent's Circus
Holmes tells Watson Mycroft is incapable of detective work

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: He is incapable of it.

events.label: Holmes clarifies that Mycroft has superior powers of observation and deduction but lacks ambition and energy

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I said that he was my superior in observation and deduction... But he has no ambition and no energy... He will not even go out of his way to verify his own solutions... Again and again I have taken a problem to him, and have received an explanation which has afterwards proved to be the correct one... And yet he was absolutely incapable of working out the practical points which must be gone into before a case could be laid before a judge or jury.

events.label: Holmes states Mycroft audits government department books and lodges at Pall Mall, walking to Whitehall each morning and evening

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: He has an extraordinary faculty for figures, and audits the books in some of the government departments... Mycroft lodges in Pall Mall, and he walks round the corner into Whitehall every morning and back every evening... From year's end to year's end he takes no other exercise, and is seen nowhere else, except only in the Diogenes Club, which is just opposite his rooms.

events.label: Holmes and Watson reach Pall Mall as they walk down it from the St. James's end
Holmes enters the club hall and cautions Watson not to speak
Holmes shows Watson into a chamber looking out into Pall Mall
Mycroft Holmes is brought into the room where Holmes and Watson are
Mycroft Holmes greets Watson and mentions expecting to see Holmes about the Manor House case

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: I am glad to meet you, sir... I hear of Sherlock everywhere since you became his chronicler... By the way, Sherlock, I expected to see you round last week, to consult me over that Manor House case. I thought you might be a little out of your depth.

events.label: Holmes responds that he solved the Manor House case and identifies Adams as the person involved

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: No, I solved it. It was Adams, of course.

events.label: Mycroft Holmes takes snuff from a tortoise-shell box and brushes away grains with a red silk handkerchief
Mycroft asks Watson and Holmes to hear about a singular problem and writes a note and hands it to the waiter

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: By the way, Sherlock, I have had something quite after your own heart—a most singular problem—submitted to my judgment... If you would care to hear the facts—

events.label: Mycroft rings the bell and asks for Mr. Melas to step across

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: I have asked Mr. Melas to step across.

events.label: Mr. Melas joins Holmes and Watson after being requested
Melas says he does not believe the police credit him and that he needs to know what happened to his man with sticking-plaster on his face

communicates.speaker: character_melas
communicates.content: I do not believe that the police credit me—on my word, I do not... But I know that I shall never be easy in my mind until I know what has become of my poor man with the sticking-plaster upon his face.

events.label: Holmes signals that he is listening to Melas

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I am all attention

events.label: Melas describes that it was Wednesday evening and that what happened was Monday night two days earlier

communicates.speaker: character_melas
communicates.content: This is Wednesday evening... it was Monday night—only two days ago

events.label: Melas states he is an interpreter associated with Greek and is the chief Greek interpreter in London

communicates.speaker: character_melas
communicates.content: I am an interpreter... I interpret all languages—or nearly all—but as I am a Greek by birth and with a Grecian name, it is with that particular tongue that I am principally associated. For many years I have been the chief Greek interpreter in London, and my name is very well known in the hotels.

events.label: Melas recounts being asked to accompany Mr. Latimer in a cab that was waiting at his door

communicates.speaker: character_melas
communicates.content: on Monday night... a Mr. Latimer... asked me to accompany him in a cab which was waiting at the door... bustling me rapidly into the cab

events.label: Latimer departs in a cab through Charing Cross and up Shaftesbury Avenue; Melas references Oxford Street before the route proceeds to Kensington
Latimer draws a lead-loaded bludgeon, places it beside Melas, and covers the carriage windows with paper
Latimer tells Melas he is sorry to cut off his view and that he has no intention for him to see the destination

communicates.speaker: character_latimer
communicates.content: I am sorry to cut off your view, Mr. Melas... The fact is that I have no intention that you should see what the place is to which we are driving... It might possibly be inconvenient to me if you could find your way there again.

events.label: Latimer warns Melas that raising an alarm or acting against his interests will be serious and says no one knows where Melas is

communicates.speaker: character_latimer
communicates.content: if at any time to-night you attempt to raise an alarm or do anything which is against my interests, you will find it a very serious thing... no one knows where you are, and that, whether you are in this carriage or in my house, you are equally in my power.

events.label: Latimer draws a blue curtain across the glass work while the carriage continues driving with windows covered and light blocked
Melas leaves Pall Mall and after timed travel arrives at a standstill near an arched doorway with a lamp
Latimer drives Melas into a house and swings open the doorway; Melas enters inside
A man in the house addresses Melas as Harold and says they could not get on without him

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: Mr. Melas, Harold? 'Yes.' 'Well done, well done! No ill-will, Mr. Melas, I hope, but we could not get on without you.'

events.label: The house host tells Melas that dealing fair will not be regretted and warns that trying tricks will lead to dire consequences

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: If you deal fair with us you'll not regret it, but if you try any tricks, God help you!'

events.label: The house host says Melas is needed to ask questions of a visiting Greek gentleman and to provide answers as instructed

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: Only to ask a few questions of a Greek gentleman who is visiting us, and to let us have the answers. But say no more than you are told to say, or... you had better never have been born.

events.label: The house host shows Melas into a richly furnished room and motions him to sit under a lamp
A younger man returns and leads in a deadly pale, emaciated gentleman with sticking-plaster criss-crossed on his face and a pad over his mouth
Mycroft Holmes states that the Diogenes Club is a spot to study mankind and points out the billiard-marker and another man approaching the window

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: To any one who wishes to study mankind this is the spot... Look at the magnificent types! Look at these two men who are coming towards us, for example.

events.label: Holmes sits with Mycroft in the bow-window of the club
Two men stop opposite the club window and one has chalk marks over the waistcoat pocket while the other has packages under his arm
Holmes and Mycroft identify the small dark fellow as having characteristics of an old soldier recently discharged from India and an artillery non-commissioned officer

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: An old soldier, I perceive.

events.label: Mycroft and Holmes discuss the small dark fellow's mourning, shopping, and children-related items seen under his arm

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: Then, of course, his complete mourning shows that he has lost some one very dear... He is doing his own shopping... He has been buying things for children... There is a rattle... The fact that he has a picture-book under his arm...

events.label: Holmes remarks that the gentleman with sticking-plaster mouth is a soldier-like figure and then recounts timetables to Melas earlier in the story

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: it is not hard to say that a man with that bearing, expression of authority, and sunbaked skin, is a soldier, is more than a private, and is not long from India.

events.label: Holmes and Mycroft reference where Mycroft is seen and club rules including no member notice and talking restrictions

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: No member is permitted to take the least notice of any other one. Save in the Stranger's Room, no talking is, under any circumstances, allowed, and three offences, if brought to the notice of the committee, render the talker liable to expulsion.

events.label: An older man cries as a strange being falls rather than sits in a chair
A speaker tells someone to give the pencil
A speaker orders Mr. Melas to ask questions and a man to write answers
A speaker asks whether the man is prepared to sign papers

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: Ask him first of all whether he is prepared to sign the papers?

events.label: A man giggles in a venomous way
A man asks what awaits the other person

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: You know what awaits you, then?

events.label: The narrator repeatedly asks whether the man will give in and sign documents
A happy thought comes to the narrator
The narrator adds sentences to each question to test companions' knowledge

communicates.content: Who are you?

communicates.speaker: character_greek_gentleman_visiting

events.label: A speaker asks how long the man has been there

communicates.speaker: character_x
communicates.content: How long have you been here?

events.label: A man states he has been there three weeks

communicates.speaker: character_greek_gentleman_visiting
communicates.content: Let it be so. Three weeks.

events.label: A speaker tells the man he will go free if he signs

communicates.speaker: character_x
communicates.content: You shall go free if you sign.

events.label: A speaker asks what house this is

communicates.speaker: character_x
communicates.content: What house is this?

events.label: The man refuses to sign and says he does not know the house

communicates.speaker: character_greek_gentleman_visiting

events.label: A speaker asks the man's name

communicates.speaker: character_x
communicates.content: What is your name?

events.label: The man says his name is Kratides

communicates.speaker: character_greek_gentleman_visiting
communicates.content: Let me hear her say so. Kratides.

events.label: A speaker asks where the man is from

communicates.speaker: character_x
communicates.content: Where are you from?

events.label: The man says he is from Athens and will never see her

communicates.speaker: character_greek_gentleman_visiting
communicates.content: Then I shall never see her. Athens.

events.label: The door opens and a woman steps into the room
The woman tells Harold she could not stay away longer and speaks about God and Paul

communicates.speaker: character_house_host_young_man
communicates.content: Harold... I could not stay away longer. It is so lonely up there with only—Oh, my God, it is Paul!

events.label: The man tears plaster from his lips and screams 'Sophy!'

communicates.speaker: character_house_host_young_man
communicates.content: Sophy!

events.label: The man rushes into the woman's arms
The younger man seizes the woman and pushes her out of the room while the elder drags the emaciated man away
The narrator is left alone in the room and springs to his feet
The older man stands in the doorway with eyes fixed upon the narrator
The older man tells Mr. Melas he will do, and that they took him into confidence

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: That will do, Mr. Melas. You perceive that we have taken you into our confidence over some very private business. We should not have troubled you, only that our friend who speaks Greek and who began these negotiations has been forced to return to the East. It was quite necessary for us to find some one to take his place, and we were fortunate in hearing of your powers.

events.label: The older man says there are five sovereigns as a sufficient fee

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: There are five sovereigns here... which will, I hope, be a sufficient fee.

events.label: The older man warns if he speaks of this to any human soul, God may have mercy on his soul

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: if you speak to a human soul about this—one human soul, mind—well, may God have mercy upon your soul!

events.label: The older man says they will know if the narrator speaks of this

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: We shall know if you speak of this... We have our own means of information.

events.label: The older man tells the narrator the carriage is waiting and friend will see him on his way

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: Now you will find the carriage waiting, and my friend will see you on your way.

events.label: The narrator is hurried through the hall and into the vehicle
Mr. Latimer follows closely and takes a place opposite the narrator
They drive in silence for a long distance until just after midnight when the carriage pulls up
The coachman lashes the horse and the carriage rattles away as the narrator springs out
Someone approaches in the darkness and is identified as a railway porter
The railway porter says the place is Wandsworth Common

communicates.speaker: character_railway_porter_placeholder
communicates.content: Wandsworth Common.

events.label: The railway porter directs the narrator to walk to Clapham Junction for the last train to Victoria

communicates.speaker: character_railway_porter_placeholder
communicates.content: If you walk on a mile or so to Clapham Junction, you'll just be in time for the last to Victoria.

events.label: The narrator tells the whole story to Mr. Mycroft Holmes next morning and subsequently to the police
Mycroft reads the advertisement seeking information about Paul Kratides from Athens who cannot speak English

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: Anybody supplying any information to the whereabouts of a Greek gentleman named Paul Kratides, from Athens, who is unable to speak English, will be rewarded.

events.label: Mycroft reads the advertisement seeking information about a Greek lady whose first name is Sophy

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: A similar reward paid to any one giving information about a Greek lady whose first name is Sophy.

events.label: The narrator notes the advertisement appeared in all the dailies and no answer came
The conversation proceeds after 'No answer'
A speaker asks how about the Greek Legation

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: How about the Greek Legation?

events.label: Mycroft says the Greek Legation knows nothing

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: I have inquired. They know nothing.

events.label: Mycroft tells Sherlock to take the case up by all means and let him know if it does any good

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: Well, you take the case up by all means, and let me know if you do any good.

events.label: Sherlock warns that Melas must be on guard because the men must know through advertisements that he betrayed them

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: In the meantime, Mr. Melas, I should certainly be on my guard, if I were you, for of course they must know through these advertisements that you have betrayed them.

events.label: Holmes stops at a telegraph office and sends off several wires
Watson suggests the Greek girl was carried off by Harold Latimer

communicates.speaker: character_x
communicates.content: It seemed to me to be obvious that this Greek girl had been carried off by the young Englishman named Harold Latimer.

events.label: Watson says the girl is not told of her brother's arrival and finds it out by accident

communicates.speaker: character_x
communicates.content: The girl is not told of the arrival of her brother, and finds it out by the merest accident.

events.label: Holmes cries 'Excellent, Watson!'

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Excellent, Watson!

events.label: Holmes says they hold all the cards and only fear some sudden act of violence

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You see that we hold all the cards, and we have only to fear some sudden act of violence on their part.

events.label: Mycroft greets Sherlock and Watson at Baker Street

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: Come in, Sherlock! Come in, sir

events.label: Mycroft says he had an answer to his advertisement

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: I had an answer to my advertisement.

events.label: Mycroft asks what effect it had
Mycroft produces a sheet of paper written with a J pen on royal cream paper by a middle-aged man with a weak constitution
The letter content is read: the writer knows the young lady and says she lives at The Myrtles, Beckenham

communicates.speaker: character_mycroft_holmes
communicates.content: Sir... I beg to inform you that I know the young lady in question very well. If you should care to call upon me I could give you some particulars as to her painful history. She is living at present at The Myrtles, Beckenham. Yours faithfully, J. Davenport.

events.label: Mycroft says the letter was written from Lower Brixton
Holmes says they know a man is being done to death and every hour may be vital

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We know that a man is being done to death, and every hour may be vital.

events.label: Watson suggests better pick up Mr. Melas on their way

communicates.speaker: character_x
communicates.content: Better pick up Mr. Melas on our way.

communicates.speaker: character_house_host

events.label: Mycroft asks whether the gentleman gave a name

communicates.content: Did the gentleman give a name?

communicates.content: No, sir.

communicates.content: He wasn't a tall, handsome, dark young man?

communicates.speaker: character_house_host
communicates.content: He was a little gentleman, with glasses, thin in the face, but very pleasant in his ways, for he was laughing all the time that he was talking.

events.label: Holmes cries 'Come along!'

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Come along!

events.label: After arriving at Scotland Yard it takes more than an hour to get Inspector Gregson and complete legal formalities to enter the house

communicates.speaker: character_inspector_gregson_placeholder

events.label: Holmes says a carriage heavily loaded with luggage passed out during the last hour

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: A carriage heavily loaded with luggage has passed out during the last hour.

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You may have observed the same wheel-tracks going the other way... But the outward-bound ones were very much deeper—so much so that we can say for a certainty that there was a very considerable weight on the carriage.

communicates.speaker: character_inspector_gregson_placeholder

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes

communicates.content: Well, I think that under the circumstances we may enter without an invitation.

Holmes rushes to the door and into the hall

events.label: The group rushes to the poisoned men and drags them into the well-lit hall
A person stops moaning when being laid down by others

The Greek interpreter acts as interpreter in a second interview after being taken to Beckenham
Two men throw the interpreter back into prison, reproach Melas with treachery from a newspaper advertisement, and stun him with a stick blow
The narrators learn that the unfortunate young lady came of a wealthy Grecian family and had visited friends in England
A young man named Harold Latimer persuades a young lady to fly with him
The young lady's friends inform her brother at Athens and then stop involvement with the matter
The brother arrives in England and places himself in Latimer's power together with Latimer's associate Wilson Kemp
Latimer and Wilson Kemp keep the brother prisoner and attempt to force him to sign away property

A newspaper cutting reaches the narrators from Buda-Pesth months later
The newspaper cutting tells of two Englishmen traveling with a woman who met a tragic end
The newspaper cutting reports that Hungarian police opined the Englishmen quarreled and inflicted mortal injuries on each other
A narrator states Holmes holds that if the Grecian girl could be found, one might learn how wrongs were avenged

clues.significance: The narrator reported that Melas's visitor drew a life-preserver from a sleeve to impress fear of instant and inevitable death.
Latimer and Wilson Kemp reproached Melas with treachery that appeared in a newspaper advertisement.
Latimer and Wilson Kemp stunned Melas with a blow from a stick, leading to Melas remembering nothing more until he found the narrators bending over him.
The plaster over the face was used to make recognition difficult in case the girl should catch a glimpse of the interpreter.
